title: Cross-hardware runner: engine extras, device auto-detect, one command
description: Copy the lm-evaluation-harness pattern: named backends, pip extras per engine, --device auto/mps/cpu/cuda, ONNX or GGUF fallback where a model ships one, a smoke test that loads each installed engine on one text. Document CUDA-only engines (NanoJev, Geni-S1-Ops, DiffusionGemma-derived) as not runnable here.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Cross-hardware runner auto-detects the device with one command

Scenario: Each installed engine passes a one-text smoke test
  Given named backends with a pip extra per engine, and CUDA-only engines (NanoJev, Geni-S1-Ops, DiffusionGemma-derived) documented as not runnable here
  When I run bd run --device auto on a task with a given engine installed
  Then it selects mps, cpu or cuda automatically, falls back to ONNX or GGUF where the model ships one, and the smoke test loads each installed engine on one text before the full run starts

right_now_summary: The runner is being built to auto-select hardware, support engine extras, and smoke-test each installed backend.
